title: Paridyum Repository Class Registry
description: The complete set of repository classes, declared under C-0005. C-0002 held this list in a locked prose table, which made every new class cost a supersession of the naming constitution. The rule stays in C-0005; the list lives in the registry. The classless `knowledge` repository is deliberately absent — it is governed by the org-scoped set (ADR-0015).

version.description: Registry format version. Bump only for a breaking shape change, which needs an ADR.

classes.description: One entry per repository class, sorted by `class`. Uniqueness of `class`, `prefix` and `scope` is enforced by the gate, not expressible here.

class.description: The class name, used as the `class` value in manifest.yaml.

prefix.description: The repository name prefix, trailing hyphen included. C-0005 fixes the grammar `<prefix><name>`; this fixes the set of prefixes.

scope.description: The value artifacts use in `scope` to bind this class. Generates knowledge.schema.json's scope enum. `org` is not a class and never appears here — it is the selector that matches every repository (ADR-0015).

deployable.description: True when this class ships a running workload, and therefore binds the Kubernetes standard. Replaces ADR-0003's applies_to prefix glob — a glob in a locked artifact can never be extended to a new prefix, which is the defect this registry exists to fix.

ci.description: True when this class uses the shared reusable CI workflow. Replaces ADR-0010's applies_to prefix glob, for the same reason.

description.description: One sentence stating what a repository of this class contains. If it needs an 'and', it is probably two classes (ANTI-0006's test, applied to classes).

declared.description: When the class entered the registry. Never changes.

notes.description: Hazards, preserved gaps, or the reasoning behind a non-obvious value. Not the rationale for the class existing; that belongs in the artifact that introduced it.

stacks.description: The language toolchains PERMITTED for this class. A set rather than one value, because a class and a stack are independent axes: `mobile` is React Native on `typescript` and Flutter on `dart`, the same class either way; `library` is a shared crate on `rust` or a shared package on `typescript`. A repository picks one and declares it in manifest.yaml as `stack`. Standards bind a stack, so a class with two stacks inherits both sets and neither leaks into the other. `none` for classes with no compiled source of their own.
